disease_label_per_paper: Hodgkin lymphoma initially diagnosed and treated as adult-onset Still's disease
presentation_summary: Ten months of recurring fever without infectious signs, with joint pain and ankle swelling
At second admission: evening recurring fever, asthenia, muscle and joint pains, swollen ankles, pallor, and tachycardia

Initial labs showed ESR 119 mm/h, CRP 303 mg/L, WBC 18 x10^9/L with 86% granulocytes, platelets 819 x10^9/L, hemoglobin 5.3 mmol/L, ferritin 1952 ng/mL, ALT 50 U/L, GGT 94 U/L, hypoalbuminemia by proteinogram, and hypergammaglobulinemia
After steroid and immunosuppressive treatment, inflammatory markers and anemia persisted; repeat imaging showed widened mediastinum and chest CT lymph node packets
Video-assisted thoracoscopic lymph node biopsy finally diagnosed Hodgkin lymphoma

quality_warnings: This is intentionally a very hard mimic case: Hodgkin lymphoma presented like AOSD and only became clear after persistent inflammation and mediastinal lymphadenopathy.
Lymph node histology is stored as confirmatory_findings, not as ordinary diagnostic evidence.
Some observations come from the re-evaluation point after several weeks of nonresponse, before the diagnostic lymph node biopsy.
